html:
Cameroon is a country in Central Africa where the coast of West Africa turns south, with Yaoundé as its capital. It gained independence in 1960 and is the only African country formed from both French and British territory.

Its north was once part of Kanem-Bornu, and the western grasslands held kingdoms such as Bamum, whose king created the Bamum script. Germany ruled it as Kamerun from 1884. After World War I it was split into French Cameroon and two British strips.

  • 1960: French Cameroon independent under Ahmadou Ahidjo.
  • 1961: Southern Cameroons voted to join; the British north joined Nigeria.
  • 1972: the federation became a single state.
  • 1982: Paul Biya took over and has ruled since.
  • 1986: the Lake Nyos disaster, a burst of gas from a volcanic lake, killed about 1,700 people.
  • Since 2016: the Anglophone crisis, an armed conflict in the English-speaking west.
sum: Cameroon is a country in Central Africa where the coast of West Africa turns south, with Yaoundé as its capital. It gained independence in 1960 and is the only African country formed from both French and British territory.
